item.research_question: How does the biocompatibility of a Ti-rich medium-entropy alloy (Ti65M) compare to a Ti-alloy (TNSM) and commercially pure titanium (CP-Ti) regarding glioblastoma astrocytoma cell viability, morphology, and gene expression?
item.material_system: Ti65-Zr18-Nb16-Mo1 (Ti65M), Ti-13Nb-7Sn-4Mo (TNSM), and commercially pure titanium (CP-Ti)
item.processing_route: Arc-melting and casting system (A-028, Dawn Shine, New Taipei City, Taiwan); samples cut into discs (10 mm diameter, 1 mm height); surfaces abraded to #1500 silicon carbide papers; cleaned ultrasonically with alcohol, acetone, and deionized water
item.test_conditions: U-87 MG glioblastoma astrocytoma cells (1 × 10^4 cells) seeded on 1.2 cm diameter samples; incubated for 24 h, then replated for an additional 24 h prior to MTT tests; extracts tested via PBS wash; contact angles measured with 1μL deionized water; XRD (40 kV, 40 mA, 2θ = 20–90°); AFM (5 × 5 μm2 scanning range)
key_findings: Ti65M exhibited the highest hardness (366.5 ± 3.6 HV) and lowest average roughness (38 ± 8 nm), while CP-Ti had the lowest hardness (172.3 ± 4.4 HV) and highest roughness (94 ± 26 nm).
All three materials were hydrophilic, with CP-Ti having the lowest contact angle (46.0 ± 0.9°) compared to Ti65M (54.3 ± 2.0°).
Cell viability on Ti65M and TNSM (β structures) was considerably higher than on CP-Ti (α' structure), with viability decreasing as Ti content increased.
U-87 MG cells showed the highest number of dendrites and axons on Ti65M, with significantly fewer observed on TNSM and CP-Ti.
Expression of ERK was reduced on TNSM and CP-Ti substrates compared to Ti65M, potentially causing lower cell migration and proliferation.
Higher expression of p53 and NFkβ was observed in U-87 MG cells on CP-Ti compared to other alloys, suggesting CP-Ti may induce apoptosis.
All extract viabilities exceeded 90%, indicating low indirect cytotoxicity for all three materials.
item.mechanism: The authors propose that the superior biocompatibility of Ti65M is related to its high content of Zr and Nb elements, which are highly biocompatible and exhibit low cytotoxicity. Additionally, the metastable β-phase structure and high hardness improve wear resistance, preventing accelerated release of metal ions. The lower expression of p53 on Ti65M compared to CP-Ti suggests reduced apoptosis, while higher expression of growth factor pathway genes (RAS, ERK, S6) on Ti65M correlates with increased cell growth and migration.
item.limitations: The authors state that the mechanisms connecting surface roughness and hydrophilicity to cellular adhesion, growth, autophagy, and differentiation are not yet clear. They also note that phase structure alone is insufficient to explain viability differences and that further investigation of corrosion resistance is needed.
item.future_work: The authors propose that increased cell migration on Ti65M is a subject for further study and that further investigation of the corrosion resistance of Ti65M and TNSM will be reported in future studies.
quotes: Ti65M has an ultra-low elastic modulus (61 GPa) due to its metastable state, which is significantly lower than those of Ti-64 (110 GPa) [] and TZNTM HEA (153 GPa) [].
The higher viabilities on Ti65M and TNSM also correlated with higher surface hardness and lower roughness.
The higher expression of p53 and NFkβ in U-87 MG on CP-Ti, compared with cells on the other Ti alloys, showed that the CP-Ti may induce apoptosis.
